subject.name: Geology
subject.description: Grade 10 Geology, Semester 1 introduces students to Earth materials, minerals, rocks, and the processes that shape our planet and its resources.

content.title: Introduction to Geology
content.description: This unit introduces geology as the study of Earth, its materials, and the scientific processes used to explore the planet and its history.

concepts.title: The contribution of geology to the different domains in our lives
concepts.description: This concept focuses on the contribution of geology to the different domains in our lives and helps learners understand the key ideas behind geology through clear scientific examples and applications.

content.title: Minerals and Their Properties
content.description: This unit explains what minerals are, how they are identified, and why their physical properties matter in geology and everyday life.

concepts.title: Minerals are homogeneous solid earth materials.
concepts.description: This concept focuses on minerals are homogeneous solid earth materials. and helps learners understand the key ideas behind geology through clear scientific examples and applications.

concepts.title: Minerals have distinct physical properties that enable them to be distinguished from one another.
concepts.description: This concept focuses on minerals have distinct physical properties that enable them to be distinguished from one another. and helps learners understand the key ideas behind geology through clear scientific examples and applications.

concepts.title: For most common minerals, the most useful properties for hand sample identification include hardness, cleavage or fracture patterns, translucency, and color.
concepts.description: This concept focuses on for most common minerals, the most useful properties for hand sample identification include hardness, cleavage or fracture patterns, translucency, and color. and helps learners understand the key ideas behind geology through clear scientific examples and applications.

concepts.title: Metallic minerals are uncommon, but economically important.
concepts.description: This concept focuses on metallic minerals are uncommon, but economically important. and helps learners understand the key ideas behind geology through clear scientific examples and applications.

concepts.title: For metallic minerals, the additional properties of streak and magnetism are useful for hand sample identification
concepts.description: This concept focuses on for metallic minerals, the additional properties of streak and magnetism are useful for hand sample identification and helps learners understand the key ideas behind geology through clear scientific examples and applications.

concepts.title: Completely unambiguous identification of minerals often requires sophisticated laboratory analysis.
concepts.description: This concept focuses on completely unambiguous identification of minerals often requires sophisticated laboratory analysis. and helps learners understand the key ideas behind geology through clear scientific examples and applications.

concepts.title: Some construction materials are highly refined from the original Earth material, while others are used in the original state.
concepts.description: This concept focuses on some construction materials are highly refined from the original earth material, while others are used in the original state. and helps learners understand the key ideas behind geology through clear scientific examples and applications.

content.title: Engineering Properties
content.description: This unit examines how Earth materials behave under stress and how their properties influence construction and engineering decisions.

concepts.title: Different Earth materials and different manufactured materials have different engineering properties, such as their behavior under stress, making them suitable for different uses in construction.
concepts.description: This concept focuses on different earth materials and different manufactured materials have different engineering properties, such as their behavior under stress, making them suitable for different uses in construction. and helps learners understand the key ideas behind geology through clear scientific examples and applications.

content.title: Igneous Rocks
content.description: This unit explores rocks formed from cooling magma or lava and the conditions that shape their appearance and texture.

concepts.title: Rocks are heterogeneous mixtures of minerals and (rarely) other earth materials.
concepts.description: This concept focuses on rocks are heterogeneous mixtures of minerals and (rarely) other earth materials. and helps learners understand the key ideas behind geology through clear scientific examples and applications.

concepts.title: Igneous rocks cooled from melts are found in association with volcanoes and also as rocks that cooled underground
concepts.description: This concept focuses on igneous rocks cooled from melts are found in association with volcanoes and also as rocks that cooled underground and helps learners understand the key ideas behind geology through clear scientific examples and applications.

concepts.title: Different cooling histories produce different igneous textures.
concepts.description: This concept focuses on different cooling histories produce different igneous textures. and helps learners understand the key ideas behind geology through clear scientific examples and applications.

concepts.title: Differences in magma composition and eruption location create differences in eruption explosivity that affect volcanic rock textures.
concepts.description: This concept focuses on differences in magma composition and eruption location create differences in eruption explosivity that affect volcanic rock textures. and helps learners understand the key ideas behind geology through clear scientific examples and applications.

content.title: Sedimentary Rocks
content.description: This unit studies rocks formed from particles, chemical deposits, and organic material, showing how environments shape their composition.

concepts.title: Sedimentary rocks that accumulate from particles can be formed in a wide range of environments on Earth's surface
concepts.description: This concept focuses on sedimentary rocks that accumulate from particles can be formed in a wide range of environments on earth's surface and helps learners understand the key ideas behind geology through clear scientific examples and applications.

concepts.title: Some sedimentary rocks form from particles of older rocks that are removed from their original location and deposited in a new one.
concepts.description: This concept focuses on some sedimentary rocks form from particles of older rocks that are removed from their original location and deposited in a new one. and helps learners understand the key ideas behind geology through clear scientific examples and applications.

concepts.title: The environment of deposition and the source material both contribute to differences in texture and composition among these sedimentary rocks.
concepts.description: This concept focuses on the environment of deposition and the source material both contribute to differences in texture and composition among these sedimentary rocks. and helps learners understand the key ideas behind geology through clear scientific examples and applications.

concepts.title: Some sedimentary rocks are made of particles from once living organisms.
concepts.description: This concept focuses on some sedimentary rocks are made of particles from once living organisms. and helps learners understand the key ideas behind geology through clear scientific examples and applications.

concepts.title: The types of organisms determine much about the texture and mineral composition of such rocks
concepts.description: This concept focuses on the types of organisms determine much about the texture and mineral composition of such rocks and helps learners understand the key ideas behind geology through clear scientific examples and applications.

concepts.title: Sedimentary rocks often contain pore spaces that make them important reservoirs of fluids in the upper part of Earth's crust.
concepts.description: This concept focuses on sedimentary rocks often contain pore spaces that make them important reservoirs of fluids in the upper part of earth's crust. and helps learners understand the key ideas behind geology through clear scientific examples and applications.

concepts.title: Sedimentary rocks sometimes contain organic material that may become part of Earth's energy resources
concepts.description: This concept focuses on sedimentary rocks sometimes contain organic material that may become part of earth's energy resources and helps learners understand the key ideas behind geology through clear scientific examples and applications.

concepts.title: Limestone and cement materials derived from limestone are essential Egyptian building resources due both to their abundance and to the lack of alternative building materials.
concepts.description: This concept focuses on limestone and cement materials derived from limestone are essential egyptian building resources due both to their abundance and to the lack of alternative building materials. and helps learners understand the key ideas behind geology through clear scientific examples and applications.

content.title: Metamorphic Rocks
content.description: This unit explains how heat and pressure transform rocks and create new mineral arrangements and textures.

concepts.title: Changes in temperature, pressure, or composition in Earth's subsurface can change the texture and mineral composition of pre-existing rocks,creating metamorphic rocks
concepts.description: This concept focuses on changes in temperature, pressure, or composition in earth's subsurface can change the texture and mineral composition of pre-existing rocks,creating metamorphic rocks and helps learners understand the key ideas behind geology through clear scientific examples and applications.

concepts.title: Deformation during metamorphism produces foliated textures and may destroy original textures.
concepts.description: This concept focuses on deformation during metamorphism produces foliated textures and may destroy original textures. and helps learners understand the key ideas behind geology through clear scientific examples and applications.

concepts.title: Deformation (change in shape) and stresses (distribution of forces) are related, but maximum deformation and maximum stress are not always parallel.
concepts.description: This concept focuses on deformation (change in shape) and stresses (distribution of forces) are related, but maximum deformation and maximum stress are not always parallel. and helps learners understand the key ideas behind geology through clear scientific examples and applications.

concepts.title: The metamorphic texture and mineralogy observed in metamorphic rocks are most commonly related to the conditions when the rock experienced its maximum temperature.
concepts.description: This concept focuses on the metamorphic texture and mineralogy observed in metamorphic rocks are most commonly related to the conditions when the rock experienced its maximum temperature. and helps learners understand the key ideas behind geology through clear scientific examples and applications.

content.title: Rock Cycle and Geological History
content.description: This unit connects the rock cycle to Earth’s long history, showing how processes continuously reshape the planet over time.

concepts.title: The rock cycle is a group of processes that act on the different types of rocks and change rocks from one form to another over geologic time
concepts.description: This concept focuses on the rock cycle is a group of processes that act on the different types of rocks and change rocks from one form to another over geologic time and helps learners understand the key ideas behind geology through clear scientific examples and applications.

concepts.title: Rock composition and texture provides evidence that can be interpreted to yield a geologic history
concepts.description: This concept focuses on rock composition and texture provides evidence that can be interpreted to yield a geologic history and helps learners understand the key ideas behind geology through clear scientific examples and applications.

concepts.title: Interpreting cross sections to study the age relationships of different rock units.
concepts.description: This concept focuses on interpreting cross sections to study the age relationships of different rock units. and helps learners understand the key ideas behind geology through clear scientific examples and applications.

concepts.title: Interpreting different geological maps that show outcrops of different rocks of Egypt.
concepts.description: This concept focuses on interpreting different geological maps that show outcrops of different rocks of egypt. and helps learners understand the key ideas behind geology through clear scientific examples and applications.

content.title: Question Bank
content.description: This section contains practice questions and assessment activities to reinforce the geology topics studied in the semester.

content.title: Revision
content.description: This section summarizes the main geological concepts and supports revision before tests and examinations.

content.title: References
content.description: This section provides useful reference materials and additional reading for deeper geoscience study.
